title: U.S. senator says Canada should make interim tariff agreement, let Congress 'legislate' long-term deal

image.caption: Senior Democratic Sen. Chris Coons said he will be working with his colleagues to get a better tariff deal when the new Congress is sworn in, calling tariffs on national security grounds an 'insult to Canada.' (Allison Robbert/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Politics

A senior Democrat in the U.S. Senate says he thinks Canada should seek an interim trade deal with the Trump administration — and the incoming U.S. Congress will figure out something better for the long term.
Canada-U.S. trade minister says an interim deal would likely include some tariffs

Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said on Thursday that the government is seeking an interim deal with the U.S. that would see Section 232 tariffs — which covers steel, aluminum, auto and lumber — lowered and Section 338 tariffs, which came into place in September, removed entirely.
Democratic Sen. Chris Coons of Delaware told CBC's Power & Politics that if Canada can get rid of the 338 tariffs, that would "be a significant accomplishment."
"Frankly, if you can get an interim deal, I'd take it, and then put it to us in the new majority to legislate an even better deal," Coons told host David Cochrane.
If you get a deal on 338 tariffs, take it — Dems will handle the rest: U.S. sen.

The president's Republican Party suffered massive losses in the U.S. midterms and some Democrats have pledged to try to end tariffs on Canadian goods once they officially take control of the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives in January.
Coons said in a separate interview with CBC Radio's The House that removing tariffs on Canadian goods is his goal as well, though he noted that might not be shared among all Democrats.

"I know that there will be folks in my party who represent steel-producing states and who will advocate for retaining some tariffs on steel and aluminum. And I had those fights when Biden was president," Coons told host Catherine Cullen in an interview airing on Saturday.
"Section 232 tariffs are justified based on alleged national security threats. For us to impose and maintain Section 232 tariffs on Canadian imports is an insult to Canada. They should be removed."
Minister LeBlanc says Canada won’t get to zero U.S. tariffs

LeBlanc told Power & Politics that if Canada can reach an interim agreement with the Trump administration, then that would likely kickstart formal talks around reviewing the Canada-U.S.-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA).
"The Americans have been clear that if we come to an arrangement to reduce the 232 and 338 tariffs, we could also begin a formal review process that's prescribed in the CUSMA agreement," he said.

LeBlanc argued that deals other countries have struck with the U.S. have all maintained some level of tariffs and that the goal is to reduce the 232 tariffs to a point where those industries could compete globally.

items: Trump says he's working on a 'fair' trade deal with Canada

blocks.text: Sources told CBC News on Thursday that the government is seeking to reach an interim trade arrangement with the Trump administration by the end of the year.
But LeBlanc says that isn't a hard deadline.
"The idea is to get the best deal we can get for Canada as soon as possible," he said. "If it takes until January or February to get that deal, we'll do that work."
The minister said Canada shouldn't see the Democrats taking control of Congress as a "magic bullet" that will end U.S. tariffs.
